title: The North Pacific outcrop-lightening law for sigma0 26.5 oxygen fails in the Southern Hemisphere: the South Pacific surface lightened but AOU fell as Ekman downwelling rose (GLODAP, 1984-2021)
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work explained the North Pacific (NP) oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 with a law: the AOU-density profile shifts lighter by kappa = 0.41-0.71 times the late-winter lightening L of the 26.0-26.8 outcrop band. Is this law general? Approach: a pre-specified out-of-sample test in the three Southern Hemisphere (SH) subtropical gyres, with the unchanged cell-matched shift code, GLODAPv2.2023 bottles of all oceans (1984-1996, 1997-2008, 2009-2021), WOA23 decadal surface fields, ERSSTv5 and NCEP/NCAR R1 wind stress. Results: our metric reproduces the published NP (0.135 kg/m3) and NA (0.046) lightening, and with GLODAP alone the NP AOU gain on 26.5 (12.5 umol/kg, 8.9-15.1) is inside the law range (8.9-18.8). The SH outcrop bands also became lighter (South Pacific 0.073, South Atlantic 0.025, South Indian 0.037 kg/m3; the South Pacific value is thermal and ERSSTv5 confirms it). But the sign test failed: in the South Pacific, AOU on 26.5 fell by 3.6 umol/kg (-6.4 to -1.2) and O2 rose by 5.4 against a predicted AOU gain of 2.1-3.7; 1997-2008 gave the same sign. The South Atlantic did not change; the South Indian AOU rose by 3.9 (0.2 to 6.9). The South Pacific water on 26.5 became fresher with more nitrate, which is new source water, not a move along the old mixing line. Exploratory: over the South Pacific outcrop band the downward Ekman pumping rose by 50% (12.9 to 19.3 m/yr), much more than in the other basins (0-7%). In 1985-1994 only 7-13% of the NP 26.3-26.6 outcrop area was under downward Ekman pumping, against 72-100% elsewhere. With lightening, NP class outcrops lost area or disappeared, while SH outcrops moved up to 1.7 degrees toward the pole and kept their area. Interpretation: the lightening law describes the NP, where these classes outcrop in the Ekman suction zone at the gyre edge; it is not a general law, and surface-lightening scaling of thermocline O2 is not valid in the SH. Limitations: 5-14 cruises per SH region and period, sparse pre-Argo SH surface data (1995-2004 lightening not robust), one reanalysis, and wind and geometry analyses that are exploratory and added after the failed test.

display.caption: Observed AOU change on sigma0 26.5 (dots, 95% cruise bootstrap; GLODAPv2.2023) against the North Pacific outcrop-lightening law (grey bars, kappa 0.41-0.71) in five basins, for 1997-2008 and 2009-2021 against 1984-1996. L is the late-winter outcrop-band lightening.

Outcrop geometry: (a) class outcrop area kept from 1985-1994 to 2005-2022, (b) fraction of each class outcrop under downward Ekman pumping (NCEP/NCAR R1), (c) AOU change on 26.5 against lightening, with the Ekman pumping change of each basin band.
(a) Late-winter surface sigma0 change 2005-2022 minus 1985-1994 (WOA23), 26.5 contours and the 26.0-26.8 outcrop band. (b) Downward Ekman pumping change with the 1985-1994 zero wind-stress-curl line.
